title: Every Polish group has a non-trivial topological group automorphism

candidates.error_location: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (construction of the automorphism φ on H)
candidates.exact_quote: As a result, to construct the desired topological group automorphism we take any non-trivial automorphism \( \varphi \) of \( \text{span}\{x_i\}_{i<n} \) and extend it to a \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-automorphism of \( H \) by setting \( \varphi(y) = y \) for \( y \in Y \).
candidates.claim_content: Setting: G is a Boolean (every element of order ≤ 2) Polish topological group of cardinality continuum, written additively, regarded as a vector space over Z_2. {x_i}_{i<n} ⊆ G is a finite Z_2-linearly independent set, L := span{x_i}_{i<n}, and U ⊆ G is an open identity neighbourhood with the two properties: (1) for distinct x, x' ∈ L, (x+U) ∩ (x'+U) = ∅ (equivalently (U+U) ∩ L = {0}); (2) G \ (L+U) has empty interior. Y ⊆ U is a maximal (under inclusion) Z_2-linearly independent subset of U, so that U ⊆ span(Y), and H is the subgroup generated by Y ∪ {x_i}_{i<n}. The paper then claims that for any non-trivial Z_2-automorphism φ of L one obtains a well-defined Z_2-automorphism of H by declaring φ(y) = y for all y ∈ Y and φ as given on L. The claim at issue: this prescription defines a well-defined linear automorphism of H. This requires that Y ∪ {x_i}_{i<n} be linearly independent, i.e. span(Y) ∩ L = {0}, equivalently span(U) ∩ L = {0}.
candidates.suspected_defect: Property (1) only gives U ∩ L = {0} and (U+U) ∩ L = {0}; it does NOT give span(U) ∩ L = {0}. A nonzero x ∈ L can be a sum of three or more elements of U (e.g. in Z_2^ω one can take U = V_0 ∪ (a_1+V_1) ∪ (a_2+V_2) with a_1+a_2 = x_0+v, v ∈ V_0 \ (V_1+V_2), satisfying (U+U)∩L = {0} while x_0 = a_1+a_2+v ∈ span(U); any such U extends by Zorn to a maximal element of the family used in Lemma 2.3, which also satisfies (2)). Then span(Y) = span(U) meets L nontrivially, Y ∪ {x_i} is linearly dependent, and the prescription 'identity on Y, φ on L' is inconsistent (it would force φ(x_0) = x_0 while φ is supposed to be non-trivial). The proof never verifies the needed independence.

candidates.exact_quote: Note that \( \varphi \) is a homeomorphism since for any neighbourhood identity \( V \) of \( 0_H \), the identity neighbourhood \( U \cap V \) is such that \( \varphi(U \cap V) = U \cap V \subseteq V \)
candidates.claim_content: Setting as in the proof of Theorem 1.1: G is a Boolean Polish group of size continuum; {x_i}_{i<n} ⊆ G finite Z_2-independent, L = span{x_i}; U an open identity neighbourhood with (x+U)∩(x'+U)=∅ for distinct x,x' ∈ L and G\(L+U) having empty interior; Y ⊆ U a maximal Z_2-independent subset of U (so U ⊆ span(Y)); H = subgroup generated by Y ∪ {x_i}; φ: H → H is defined to be a non-trivial automorphism on L and the identity on Y. The claim is: for every neighbourhood V of 0 in H, φ(U ∩ V) = U ∩ V, hence φ is continuous at 0 and a homeomorphism.
candidates.suspected_defect: The equality φ(U ∩ V) = U ∩ V presupposes that φ fixes every point of U. That requires U ⊆ span(Y) AND φ restricted to span(Y) to be the identity, i.e. span(Y) ∩ L = {0}. But if span(U) = span(Y) meets L nontrivially (which properties (1)–(2) of U do not exclude; (1) only yields (U+U) ∩ L = {0}), elements of U may have nonzero L-component and are then moved by φ. Also, even granting φ|_U = id, the argument shows only continuity at the identity of φ and tacitly of φ^{-1}; the equality as stated is unjustified in general.

candidates.exact_quote: Theorem 3.1. A non-trivial Polish group cannot be uniquely homogeneous.
candidates.claim_content: Definition used in the paper: a space X is uniquely homogeneous if for any two points p, q ∈ X there is a unique homeomorphism of X carrying p to q. Theorem 3.1 asserts that no non-trivial (i.e. more than one element) Polish group is uniquely homogeneous. Consider the two-element discrete group G = Z_2 = {0,1}, which is a non-trivial Polish group. Its self-homeomorphisms are exactly the identity and the transposition. For p = q the only homeomorphism carrying p to q is the identity (the transposition moves p); for p ≠ q the only one is the transposition.
candidates.suspected_defect: G = Z_2 is a non-trivial Polish group that IS uniquely homogeneous, so Theorem 3.1 as stated is false. The hypothesis should be 'more than two elements', matching Theorem 1.1 ('Every Polish group with more than two elements admits a non-trivial topological automorphism'), since Aut(Z_2) is trivial.

candidates.exact_quote: We prove that every Polish group admits a non-trivial topological group automorphism.
candidates.claim_content: The abstract claims every Polish group admits a non-trivial topological group automorphism (a topological automorphism being a map that is both a group automorphism and a self-homeomorphism, and 'non-trivial' meaning different from the identity). The paper's actual theorem is: every Polish group WITH MORE THAN TWO ELEMENTS admits a non-trivial topological automorphism. The trivial group and the two-element group Z_2 have only the identity automorphism, since Aut({e}) and Aut(Z_2) are trivial.
candidates.suspected_defect: The abstract's statement is literally false for the trivial group and for Z_2; it contradicts the hypothesis 'with more than two elements' in Theorem 1.1. Similarly the abstract's 'there are no uniquely homogeneous Polish groups' fails for Z_2 (and the one-point group).

candidates.exact_quote: Now we construct a non-empty open subset V′ ⊆ V for which (x + V′) + (y + V′) = ∅ if x, y ∈ L are distinct.
candidates.claim_content: In the proof of Lemma 2.3 (G a Boolean Hausdorff topological group written additively, L = span{x_i}_{i<n} a finite subgroup, U a ⊆-maximal open identity neighbourhood with (x+U)∩(y+U)=∅ for distinct x,y ∈ L, V = int(G \ (L+U)) assumed non-empty), the paper constructs V' ⊆ V and asserts '(x + V′) + (y + V′) = ∅' and later '(x + V') + (y + V') ⊆ (x + x + U_x) ∩ (y + y + U_y) = ∅' for distinct x, y ∈ L.
candidates.suspected_defect: The operation symbol is wrong: the sum of two non-empty subsets of a group is never empty; the intended statement is (x+V') ∩ (y+V') = ∅, which is what the displayed containment in U_x ∩ U_y actually proves. As written the asserted identity is false.

candidates.exact_quote: Since \( V' \neq \varnothing \), \( W \) is an element of \( \mathbb{P} \) that strictly contains the maximal element \( U \).
candidates.claim_content: In the proof of Lemma 2.3, U is a ⊆-maximal element of the family P of open identity neighbourhoods U with (x+U)∩(y+U)=∅ for all distinct x,y in the finite subgroup L = span{x_i}_{i<n} of the Boolean Hausdorff group G; V = int(G \ (L+U)) is assumed non-empty, and V' is a non-empty open subset of V with (x+V')∩(y+V')=∅ for distinct x,y ∈ L. The paper concludes from 'V' ≠ ∅' alone that W := U ∪ V' strictly contains U.
candidates.suspected_defect: Strict containment needs V' ⊄ U, not merely V' ≠ ∅; this requires the (true but unstated) observation that V' ⊆ V ⊆ G \ (L+U) is disjoint from U (as 0 ∈ L). Likewise the cross terms (x+U)∩(y+V') = ∅ in the displayed computation of (x+W)∩(y+W) are asserted without justification. The step is incompletely justified as written.

candidates.exact_quote:
If we consider \( \varphi \) to be a con-
tinuous homomorphism from \( H \) to \( G \), then there exists a unique continuous ex-
tension \( \overline{\varphi} : G \to G \) of \( \varphi \) by the density of \( H \) in \( G \)
candidates.claim_content: Lemma 2.2 claims: if G is a Polish group and H a dense subgroup (with the subspace topology), then every topological automorphism φ of H (a group automorphism of H that is also a self-homeomorphism of H) extends uniquely to a topological automorphism of G. The proof asserts the existence of a unique continuous extension φ̄: G → G of φ by density of H in G, and likewise for φ^{-1}, then concludes φ̄ ∘ (φ^{-1})‾ = Id_G.
candidates.suspected_defect: A continuous map from a dense subspace into a complete metric space need not extend continuously; one needs uniform continuity with respect to a complete uniformity (here: continuous homomorphisms are uniformly continuous for the two-sided uniformity, and G, being Polish, is Raikov complete). This justification is omitted, and the extension φ̄ being a group homomorphism is also not argued. Worth checking whether the lemma holds in the stated generality (in particular that the extension is a homomorphism and bijective).

candidates.error_location: Introduction, remark on mapping class groups
candidates.exact_quote:
everyextendedmappingclassgroupisnaturallyisomorphic(as an abstract group)
to its automorphism group.
candidates.claim_content: The paper asserts that for extended mapping class groups of connected metrizable surfaces (and their finite-index subgroups) every algebraic automorphism is given by conjugation with a mapping class, and that consequently every extended mapping class group is naturally isomorphic (as an abstract group) to its own automorphism group.
candidates.suspected_defect: The isomorphism Aut(Γ) ≅ Γ via inner automorphisms requires Γ to have trivial centre; for several low-complexity surfaces the (extended) mapping class group has non-trivial centre or is itself trivial/abelian (e.g. sphere, torus, small exceptional cases), so the blanket statement 'every extended mapping class group' appears too strong, and in those cases the implied non-trivial inner automorphism need not exist.

candidates.error_location: Proof of Theorem 1.1, first sentence of the construction
candidates.exact_quote: Let \( \{x_i\}_{i<n} \subset G \) be a finite collection with more than two elements of \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-linearly independent elements.
candidates.claim_content: In the proof of Theorem 1.1, G is a Boolean Polish group of cardinality continuum and {x_i}_{i<n} ⊆ G is a finite Z_2-linearly independent collection; later a non-trivial Z_2-automorphism of span{x_i}_{i<n} ≅ Z_2^n is used. The hypothesis stated is that the collection has 'more than two elements'.
candidates.suspected_defect: The condition needed is n ≥ 2 (so that span{x_i} ≅ Z_2^n has a non-trivial automorphism, |GL_n(Z_2)| > 1); 'more than two elements' presumably refers to the span having more than two elements, but literally read as n > 2 it is a stronger-than-needed and ambiguous hypothesis. The correctness of the quantity (which n guarantees a non-trivial automorphism of the span) should be checked: for n = 1, Aut(Z_2) is trivial.
